sentences.text: 4. Mr Hariharan, learned senior counsel for the petitioner states that in the present case, 22 Bighas and 05 Biswas of the agricultural land has been purchased in the name of the society and the same is encumbrance free.
He also states that the said land is at the disposal of the members of the society.
5. He further states that the said land can be sold and from the money realised, apportionment of the entire amount can be done amongst the members of the society on pro rata basis.
6. Mr. Narang, learned counsel appears for the complainant and has no objection if the said land is sold and the money realised from the said land can be divided among the members of the society.

7. However, learned senior counsel for the petitioner as well as learned counsel for the complainant and the State submits that in order to ensure transparency and fair play in the process of selling the land, a Local Commissioner/Observer can be appointed who can oversee the entire process of selling and apportioning the said land.

8. Mr. Sukhdev Singh, Retd. ADJ (Mobile No. 9910384661) is appointed as the Local Commissioner/Observer to take steps to sell the land measuring about 22 Bighas and 05 Biswas in the revenue estate of village Bakhtawarpur, Delhi-110036 and thereafter, apportion the sale proceeds on pro rata basis amongst all the stakeholders/members of the society.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 06/12/2024 at 22:30:46 9.
The fee of the Local Commissioner/Observer is fixed at Rs. 1 lakh per month which will be paid on pro rata basis by all the members of the society including the petitioner.
10. Ms Gupta, learned APP states that at this stage, the investigation is complete qua the petitioner.
11. I am of the view that the petitioner has been in custody since 28.04.2024 and the investigation has been completed against the petitioner.
The charge-sheet in the present case has also been filed and at this stage, the custody of the petitioner is not required.

12. For the aforesaid reasons, the petition is allowed and the petitioner is directed to be released on regular bail in FIR No. 033/2022 registered at P. S. Economic Offence Wing under sections 420/406/409/120-B IPC, subject to the following terms and conditions:
(a) The petitioner shall furnish a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 30,000/-
